summary: Exact candidate 483b25d3c73ad38148343f4417e21262425162d5 closes the prior default-mode annotated ASCII NAME, increasing-width CJK STRING, and increasing-width CJK NAME counterexamples. STRING and non-ASCII NAME bodies do not enter the fast path. Residual work and timing remain non-quadratic, and C10 reports duplicate-safe corpus identity. The candidate is nevertheless blocking because accepted ASCII NAME and NUMBER chains still change formatting bytes at supported custom line lengths. At line_length=10, a top-level chain of 30 equal-width `[k]` trailers enters the batch helper four times and produces 284 bytes instead of the legacy path's 518 bytes, dropping the legacy optional RHS parentheses. The same drift occurs for `[0]` trailers, and an indented NAME chain drifts at line_length=17. The committed legacy differential always uses default Mode(), so it does not cover this boundary class.

CJK STRING output matched legacy at SHA-256 2cbedf18f345f6f7808421990222741cbc8a3c77016ed92a40cf73260bba1a9b with zero batch invocations. CJK NAME output matched legacy at SHA-256 5c066e5d8c14daa7a09b87b1aeaea7539f6fd805059937afdfa2dfeef2f88031 with zero batch invocations.

falsification_attempts.hypothesis: Every accepted monotonic ASCII NAME/NUMBER shape remains byte-identical to forced legacy splitting across line-length and indentation boundaries.
falsification_attempts.probe: Format top-level and indented chains of 30 equal-width ASCII NAME or NUMBER trailers with custom line lengths, track fast-path acceptance, and compare against the unchanged legacy loop by forcing the helper to raise CannotSplit.
falsification_attempts.evidence: diff.patch and replayable QA probe P2: at black.Mode(line_length=10), source SHA-256 61bcc863cb73b86130165320fe10d374781780930b16b0a3ba7fdfb5175445f0 (`result = base` plus 30 `[k]` trailers) entered the batch path four times. Candidate SHA-256 add2578319a68a9263cd022194980479cb1f0ac44349862a4080d6ada5ee259e was 284 bytes; forced legacy SHA-256 b3e902fb19a65860fdf3687f2b350044e171d2c75abc720f6631540b43cdba10 was 518 bytes. The unified diff begins with legacy `result = (` versus candidate `result = base[`, proving optional-parenthesis drift. Thirty `[0]` trailers at line_length=10 also entered four times and differed: candidate SHA-256 e0a681e14d503f2eaa8fe849b10e2ae25744eab85d4e7d27afe09a82d27cf71d versus legacy ad65b9f3b9842536fd885cc7bf601b75290a5c0567be93ffbf8559bb0f39e61f. An indented `[k]` chain at line_length=17 likewise differed, 537 bytes versus 727.

findings.claim: The ASCII NAME/NUMBER fast path changes exact formatting bytes at custom line-length boundaries by omitting legacy optional RHS parentheses.
findings.evidence: Replayable QA probe P2 used black.Mode(line_length=10) with source `result = base` plus 30 `[k]` trailers. The helper accepted four times. Candidate output was 284 bytes with SHA-256 add2578319a68a9263cd022194980479cb1f0ac44349862a4080d6ada5ee259e; forced legacy output was 518 bytes with SHA-256 b3e902fb19a65860fdf3687f2b350044e171d2c75abc720f6631540b43cdba10. The unified diff shows legacy wrapping the RHS as `result = (` while the batch result begins `result = base[`. Repeating `[0]` produced the same class of drift, and an indented ASCII NAME chain drifted at line_length=17. These shapes satisfy the exact guard in diff.patch.

findings.claim: The committed optimized-versus-legacy regression only uses default line length and therefore misses accepted ASCII boundary drift.
findings.evidence: diff.patch constructs every differential with black.Mode() and does not parameterize line_length. C11 reports zero mismatches for 290 cases, but replayable QA probe P2 finds direct accepted-path mismatches at line lengths 10 and 17 for both NAME and NUMBER bodies.
